method.fresh: One fresh process per input after resident run compiled caches; each processes one input.
method.resident: One process processes nine inputs; first call excluded from warmed medians. Three runs per clip.
method.timing: Normalized WAV input through speech/Light cleanup; excludes GUI, IPC, recovery saving, model integrity verification, and initial Python imports. Fresh workers exit after their idle sample.
method.resources: 0.1-second worker RSS/private-memory samples; CPU time divided by elapsed time and 8 logical CPUs. Two-second loaded idle samples; GPU/driver memory not fully captured.
method.background: Normal applications remained open; no graphics probe during these runs.
method.recognition: OpenVINO tiny.en INT4 default decoding vs faster-whisper tiny.en INT8, two CPU threads, beam 1 and 5. Different precision/decoding; deployment comparison, not engine-only isolation.

quality.reference: No checked audio reference; WER and accuracy ranking are unmeasured.
quality.review: Inspected all distinct saved cleanup outputs against raw text. No personal speech is included in this report.
observations: 1.5B GPU added interpretations and changed wording/tone in clip a without triggering the current guard.
1.5B CPU retained raw text for clip c after a negation-change rejection; all three resident clip-c calls fell back.
7B GPU had two final variants for clip c; two of three clip-c calls retained raw after a negation-change rejection.
Repeated CPU speech outputs were stable within each engine configuration; speech engines produced different text.
quality.decision: Keep current speech and 7B cleanup defaults. Persistent models merit an optional dictation mode; 1.5B GPU is unsuitable as default from this sample.

setup_issue: faster-whisper 1.2.1 file decoding raised TypeError with PyAV 19.0.1 metadata_errors. Comparison supplied normalized NumPy PCM to both engines instead; public application dependencies were unchanged.

graphics.method: Fixed 1280x720 WebGL2 draw, 4096x4096 texture, 32 texture samples per pixel; synchronous pixel read verifies completed rendering. Headless Chrome uses hardware Intel D3D11, renderer verified. Seven-second unloaded baseline before each worker. Two passes with reversed device order; first 7B pass used nine jobs, others five. Warm statistics exclude first job and use only the two ten-second clips. Each pass summarized separately, then medians across passes.
graphics.limits: This measures interference with one graphics workload, not GPU utilization percentage or response in every application. Worker idle windows are only two seconds. No other benchmark ran alongside this probe.
